diagnostic_interpretation: Probe1 mistakenly used CS override for the memory SMSW success fixture. Its control-only native observation was insufficient to reject the resulting GP handler halt. The corrected probe uses DS and asserts terminal RIP before comparison; no production code change masked this fixture error.

Probe2 verifies 768 original execution cases per SDK, then the direct owner stops at the existing explicit mixed-mode LMSW refusal. An independent SMSW backing test proves loss of its paid instruction continuation. These are retained pre-implementation red cases.
Green1 passes all three initial groups on both SDKs after implementation: original768, owner768, operand-resume16.

Green2 passes seven of nine expanded groups on both SDKs. Two new debug fixtures fail admission because their Legacy.Debug and Long.DebugProfile disagree; both profiles are now bound. This fixture correction changes no production rule.

Green3 passes eight of nine groups on both SDKs, including original TF/control cases. The data-comparator recovery fixture still selected DebugRegisters, whose contract excludes RW/LEN data comparators; it now consistently binds Watchpoints. No production rule changes for these fixture repairs.
Green4 passes the repaired 16-case data/TF recovery group and all 26 standalone status groups on each SDK, including 5220 original legacy comparisons per SDK.
Diagnostic runs identify their working-tree content separately from the immutable clean full qualification.

native_oracle.method: Fresh pinned local Intel KVM VM/vCPU per case; one initial SREGS write, no intermediate host mode or control rewrites. KVM backing is pre-faulted and page A/D input bits match. Compare all 16 represented GPRs, PC/flags, represented segment/control fields and every RAM byte; debug cases also compare DR0..3/6/7. Existing segment comparisons treat unusable cache fields as opaque; these fixtures use nonnull caches. No complete XSAVE or unspecified machine-bank comparison is claimed.
native_oracle.debug_preparation: The TF cases execute an original DR7 read to install the debug bank, then real guest PUSH/POPF and optional MOV-SS. Host debugging is not enabled. LMSW input4 changes EM, so these are KVM original-stream comparisons, not a claim of uninterrupted physical LMSW or hardware data-watchpoint qualification.
limitations: Only the local pinned Intel P/E cores are measured. Production code uses supplied profiles and does not infer a CPU model from the host.
The raw and direct matrices each contain 768 execution cases. CLTS ignores operand-form parameters, so these are not 768 distinct instruction encodings.
Native runs are uninterrupted. Backing pauses, contradictory full-bank changes and frozen-context policies are software contract tests against uninterrupted software baselines.
Generated observations enter code64 from compatibility16/32 by original far JMP; generated source compiles for host x64. Protected16/32 comparisons are direct original-byte owner executions.

coverage: Four non64 modes use existing shared SMSW/LMSW/CLTS rules across operand/address widths and register/memory forms. LMSW retains PE and CR0 high bits, changes only MP/EM/TS, and reads a fixed word. CLTS only clears TS.
The mode boundary admits LMSW/CLTS without duplicating CR0 calculation. CR3, CR4, EFER/LMA and active/inactive cached PDPTE banks are preserved. Publication precedes post-instruction debug delivery.

Generated HighC/LLVMC code64 at O0/O2 with host-x64 Clang/NeverC observes committed CR0 through SMSW after real compatibility-to-code64 far jumps; source operands and complete ordinary RAM are compared.
Original CPL3 and UMIP cases retain privilege-before-operand priority; instruction fetch faults precede control changes or instruction privilege faults.

A typed MachineStatus transfer marker keeps authenticated bytes and the paid attempt after an incomplete logical SMSW/LMSW operand access. It does not retain partial physical read fragments. Repeated zero-budget resume keeps the original bindings and neither refetches nor recharges the instruction.

Sixteen software operand cases cover aligned and cross-page accesses, changed accepted bytes, full-bank rejection and frozen profiles. Sixteen software debug cases repair the operand and then suspend at IDT or frame backing, preserving the single completion and committed controls before combined data/TF delivery.

Standalone shared-owner negatives reject changed Scalars/MachineStatus bindings without consuming the marker. Operand retry to guest PF retires the instruction marker before suspended event entry; event-only resume retains the fault PC and no completion.

Regression includes full paging, paged source, legacy source, instruction-boundary and SDK source integration on both SDKs. Full paging replays all existing Far/Return/Segment continuation consumers after the shared journal change.
boundaries: NeverC remains host/source x64. No 32-bit source target is restored.

This closes mixed-mode machine-status integration and its paid logical operand attempts, not all non64 state owners. Ports/strings/MPX, legacy returns, task/system selectors, descriptor queries, fast-system entry, call gates and VM86 composition remain separate work.
Cross-line event accessed updates, further machine transitions, software SMM/SGX, unbound asynchronous producers and physical SGX qualification remain open.
Production LLVM remains neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6. No final release, pin or LLVM source gitlink change.

compiled_source_followup.scope: Test-only compiled SMSW/LMSW paid operand resume, without production changes.
compiled_source_followup.method: Eight software cases per compiler/optimization parameter cover legacy and PAE paging, guest16/32 and SMSW/LMSW. Both x64 Clang and x64 NeverC run at O0/O2. Interrupted generated C is compared with the same compiled uninterrupted baseline, full GPR/control/RAM state and exact accounting.
compiled_source_followup.coverage: Retain paid instruction across missing operand backing, reject changed accepted machine-status binding, retry twice at zero budget after host opcode mutation, then reconstruct both physical memory and execution context. Complete once without re-fetch or another attempt. The final PTE A/D effects match the uninterrupted baseline.
compiled_source_followup.limitations: This is software C-bridge recovery evidence, not native hardware interruption or physical-fragment retention. Counts are separate from the preceding clean full regression.
